mechanics.summary: Making a selected location livable typically takes one or more shifts and requires one SURVIVAL roll and one STAMINA roll; each is made by one person, may be helped, and may be retried once per shift.
trigger: group establishes home base
exceptions: Quartermaster modifies the Survival roll and Builder modifies the Stamina roll.
Exact cleaning and habitability time is Referee-determined.

unknowns: Location suitability and exact time are Referee determinations.

mechanics.summary: An established home base allows the group to sleep and rest there without Survival rolls to make camp.
trigger: group sleeps or rests at established home base

unknowns: Whether the location is the established home base requires campaign state.

mechanics.summary: Each week, spend one shift on home-base repairs and general upkeep and make a STAMINA roll.
trigger: home-base upkeep week occurs
exceptions: Builder modifies the roll. One person rolls, others may help; one roll per shift and multiple attempts are allowed.

unknowns: Weekly timing and helper eligibility require tracking and input.

mechanics.summary: If a full week passes without successful upkeep, the home base no longer provides basic shelter and its two establishment rolls must be made again.
trigger: one full week passes without successful upkeep

value.require: repeat Survival and Stamina establishment rolls

unknowns: Upkeep success history requires tracking.

mechanics.summary: Adding a facility uses its printed prerequisites, work time, and skill rolls. Time assumes two work shifts per day; one person rolls each skill, helpers may assist, failed construction may be retried after spending the same time, and multiple units of a facility may be added.
trigger: group builds home-base facility
exceptions: Further facilities and site suitability require Referee approval or determination.

unknowns: Site suitability and additional facilities require Referee input.

mechanics.summary: A cow pen holds one cow. Milking once per day takes one shift and yields 2D6 domestic-food rations; slaughtering takes one shift and yields 2D6x6 domestic-food rations.
trigger: cow in cow pen is milked or slaughtered
exceptions: Eating uncooked slaughtered meat requires a Stamina roll against food poisoning.

unknowns: Cow presence and food cooking require tracking.

mechanics.summary: For each success on a fall cropland harvest, yield D6x100 wild-food units. Establishment needs one week, tending needs one shift per spring/summer week, and both establishment and harvest use STAMINA.
trigger: cropland is established, tended, or harvested

unknowns: Season and cultivation state require tracking.

mechanics.summary: Defenses provide defensive positions with cover of armor level 3 or higher.
trigger: facility defenses are used in base combat

unknowns: Exact layout and armor level above 3 are not specified.

mechanics.summary: A heater eliminates cold effects in the home base.
trigger: home base has operating heater

unknowns: Operating fuel/firewood state requires tracking.

mechanics.summary: An infirmary gives +1 to MEDICAL AID rolls in addition to medical-gear modifiers.
trigger: Medical Aid roll occurs in infirmary

mechanics.summary: A garage gives +1 to TECH rolls repairing vehicles and can be used for construction.
trigger: Tech repairs vehicle in garage

mechanics.summary: A lookout gives +1 to spot enemies approaching the base and provides cover with armor level 2.
trigger: base occupant spots approaching enemy or uses lookout cover

unknowns: Approaching-enemy state requires Referee input.

mechanics.summary: A pigsty holds up to twelve pigs. Slaughtering a pig takes one shift and yields 2D6x2 domestic-food rations.
trigger: pig in pigsty is slaughtered
exceptions: Eating uncooked meat requires a Stamina roll against food poisoning.

unknowns: Pig inventory and cooking require tracking.

mechanics.summary: Prison cells hold up to twelve prisoners behind armor-level-2 doors.
trigger: prison cells hold prisoners or doors are attacked

mechanics.summary: Domestic food stored in a root cellar lasts one month instead of one week before spoiling.
trigger: domestic food is stored in root cellar

unknowns: Elapsed storage time requires tracking.

mechanics.summary: A religious person spending one shift at a shrine recovers one additional stress point; a shrine can be used once per day.
trigger: religious person spends shift at shrine

unknowns: Religious-person status requires input.

mechanics.summary: A well gives everyone in the home base free access to clean water.
trigger: base has well

outcome.value: access clean water without resource cost

unknowns: Base membership requires input.

mechanics.summary: Each day, a windmill produces power on D6 3+ for one large electric device or up to twelve small electric devices.
trigger: day begins at base with windmill

value.power: one large or up to twelve small devices

unknowns: Device sizes and active demand require tracking.

mechanics.summary: A workshop gives +1 to TECH repair rolls except vehicle repairs and can be used for construction.
trigger: Tech repairs nonvehicle item in workshop
exceptions: Does not apply to vehicle repairs; garage covers those.

mechanics.summary: A garage and workshop permit manufacture of vehicles and mechanical gear, including weapons and ammunition. Manufacturing requires a difficult -2 TECH roll and applicable specialty bonuses.
trigger: actor manufactures item in garage and workshop
exceptions: Applicable specialty may be Blacksmith, Gunsmith, Mechanic, Electrician, or Chemist.

unknowns: Applicable specialty and item classification require input.

mechanics.summary: Successful manufacture creates reliability two below original, minimum 1, plus one per success after the first up to original reliability; this result is the item's maximum reliability.
trigger: manufacturing Tech roll succeeds

outcome.value: min(original, max(1, original - 2) + successes after first); set as item maximum reliability

unknowns: Original item reliability requires reference data.

mechanics.summary: Manufacturing a weapon takes about one week for small arms or several weeks for heavy weapons and consumes general and weapon spare parts of equal weight totaling the weapon's weight; electronics may also be required at Referee discretion.
trigger: actor manufactures weapon

value.materials: equal general and weapon spare-part weight totaling weapon weight
value.time: about one week small arms; several weeks heavy weapons

exceptions: Electronic spare parts are Referee discretion.

unknowns: Exact time and electronics requirement require Referee input.

mechanics.summary: Ammunition needs equal general-spare-part and explosive weight totaling ammunition weight. Each TECH success produces one encumbrance unit per shift; on failure reroll immediately, and a second failure triggers an explosion.
trigger: actor manufactures ammunition in workshop

value.materials: equal general spare parts and explosives totaling ammunition weight
value.output: one encumbrance unit per success per shift

unknowns: Explosion effects require applicable explosive context.

mechanics.summary: Manufacturing a vehicle takes about one week for a bicycle or motorcycle or several weeks for larger vehicles and consumes equal general and vehicle spare-part weight totaling vehicle weight; most vehicles also need electronic parts, and mounted weapons are built separately.
trigger: actor manufactures vehicle

value.materials: equal general and vehicle spare-part weight totaling vehicle weight
value.time: about one week bicycle/motorcycle; several weeks larger vehicles

exceptions: Most vehicles require electronic spare parts.
Vehicle-mounted weapons are not included and must be made separately in a workshop.

unknowns: Exact time and electronic-parts requirement require item data and Referee input.

cropland.time: one week establish; one shift per spring/summer week tend; one week fall harvest

heater.prerequisites: basic tools; firewood or 5 liters alcohol fuel/day

windmill.prerequisites: basic tools; 40 general and 40 electronic spare parts

referenceData.notes: Still and generator refer to printed jury-rigging rules on page 131, outside this batch scope.
Examples supplement the general weight-based materials procedure.
